analysis.title: Downgrade of global equities to a Core allocation
key_insights: Standard Chartered's Global CIO Office downgrades global equities from Overweight to Neutral/Core. Fixed income stays Neutral, Gold stays Overweight, Cash stays Underweight.
For the CIO Foundation Balanced portfolio, the equity allocation falls to 52.5% from 53.2%, a small cut.

The bank still expects positive global equity returns over the next 6-12 months but says investors should lower expectations from the 15-20% annualised gains of recent years. Its capital market assumptions point to mid-to-high single digit annual returns over the next few years, consistent with a move to a mid-cycle bull market.
Consensus expects 16% earnings growth for global equities in 2027, which the bank says should outweigh headwinds and deliver positive 12-month returns.
The bank stays Overweight US and Asia ex-Japan equities because they are expected to have the highest 2027 earnings growth among major regions, led by technology, the largest sector weight in both.
Core allocations are held on Euro area equities (lower valuations) and Japan (reflating economy). UK is Underweight because its sector mix gives lower 2027 growth.

Within Asia ex-Japan, Taiwan (semiconductor-driven structural growth) and India (diversified non-tech growth) are Overweight, and both generate attractive returns on equity. China (low valuations) and Korea (explosive semiconductor earnings growth but volatile prices) are Core. ASEAN is Underweight on lower earnings growth.
Overweight sectors globally: US information technology, US healthcare, US financials, US materials, Europe ex-UK financials, and Japan financials.

The bank expects the US tech block (IT, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary) to deliver about 30% earnings growth in 2027, extending 2026 momentum. Financials and Real Estate are expected at low-teens growth, Resources (Industrials, Materials, Energy, Utilities) at 10-15% with Energy the largest drag, and Healthcare & Staples at mid-teens with a possible healthcare upside surprise.

The downgrade is partly framed as reflecting a broadening of market leadership away from tech toward the other three sector blocks. The bank says diversification across sectors and regions matters more as AI moves from buildout toward monetisation.

Opportunistic equity ideas are Global High-Dividend, US healthcare, Euro area banks, MSCI Switzerland and Japan banks. They have an average beta below 1 versus MSCI AC World. US healthcare (12-Oct-26) and MSCI Switzerland (29-Oct-26) are new.
The bank argues for more active management in a mid-cycle transition because higher dispersion should create more opportunity in sector and stock selection.

The bank expects more frequent volatility from a more uncertain political backdrop and maturing growth in some segments. It suggests structured strategies for income, discounted entry prices, or full or partial principal return at maturity.
For moderating equity returns, the bank suggests equity long/short hedge funds, private equity and infrastructure for investors who can accept illiquidity.

After this year's surge in bond yields, the bank says bonds now hedge equity weakness. It prefers the 3-7 year part of the US curve against an AI-growth-worry sell-off, since that part has priced in most Fed rate hike expectations, which could reverse if growth concerns return.
The bank favours US TIPS as a hedge against a fuel price-led inflation scare.

In credit, a defensive stance means higher-rated issuers and secured over subordinated debt. Large diversified banks, utilities and quasi-sovereigns are seen as more defensive than cyclical sectors such as metals and mining, exploration and technology.
Tactical FX hedge: bearish AUD/JPY. Across 21 past S&P 500 correction sessions (2010-2025), AUD fell against USD in 86% and JPY rose against USD in 67%.

sector_views.rationale: Tech block expected to deliver about 30% US earnings growth in 2027.
Supported by obesity treatment adoption, oncology advances and medical devices. Also a new opportunistic idea. Healthcare earnings rebound is a possible upside surprise.
Financials and Real Estate block expected to grow earnings at a low-teens rate in 2027 on resilient activity and healthy credit trends.
Part of the Resources block, expected at 10-15% earnings growth in 2027.
Euro area banks show steady earnings growth, adding to excess capital returned through dividends and buybacks.
Net margin expansion from BoJ policy normalisation and corporate governance improvements.
Likely the largest drag on Resources earnings growth in 2027 due to tougher comparisons and softer energy price assumptions.

earnings_insights: Consensus estimates point to 16% earnings growth for global equities in 2027 (consensus estimate, not a print).
US and Asia ex-Japan are expected to have the highest 2027 consensus earnings growth among major regions.
The bank expects about 30% US tech block earnings growth in 2027 (bank estimate), extending 2026 momentum.
The bank expects low-teens 2027 earnings growth for Financials and Real Estate, 10-15% for Resources, and mid-teens for Healthcare & Staples (bank estimates).
Korea is described as having explosive earnings growth in semiconductors, with volatile price movements.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus growth should overcome headwinds and support positive 12-month equity returns.
The bank's index target implies roughly 9% upside.
The bank says this year's yield surge means bonds now offer a hedge against equity weakness.
Below the 15-20% annualised gains of recent years, supporting the call to lower return expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects 16% global earnings growth in 2027, led by technology and healthcare, enough to overcome headwinds and deliver positive 12-month returns. The bank's S&P 500 target implies about 9% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Returns are expected to moderate from the 15-20% annualised pace of recent years, to mid-to-high single digits. Political uncertainty and maturing growth in some segments could bring more volatility, and AI-related growth worries could cause a sell-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A return of growth concerns that reverses priced-in Fed rate hike expectations is the stated trigger for the bond hedge to work, signalling equity stress.

theme_stances.key_argument: Equity investors may need to recalibrate expectations lower from the 15-20% annualised gains of recent years, though returns should stay positive.
